# onetsolutions_hosting_database_privileges (Resource)

Grants a MySQL user of a web hosting privileges on one of its databases.

The privileges replace whatever the user had on the database, and change in place. They cannot be
read back: a refresh only checks the user still has privileges on the database, and recreates the
resource when it has none. After an import, the next apply sets the configured privileges.

~> **Destroying does not revoke.** Destroying the resource only removes it from the Terraform
state: the privileges stay granted until the user or the database is deleted, or other privileges
are set. `terraform plan` warns before it does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

variable "database_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_database" "shop" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  name       = "shop"
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_database_user" "app" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  username   = "app"
  password   = var.database_password
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_database_privileges" "app_on_shop" {
  hosting_id = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  database   = onetsolutions_hosting_database.shop.name
  username   = onetsolutions_hosting_database_user.app.username
  privileges = ["SELECT", "INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"]

  lifecycle {
    # A new password recreates the user, which drops its privileges: grant them again.
    replace_triggered_by = [onetsolutions_hosting_database_user.app]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `database` (String) The name of the database, with or without the web hosting's username prefix, such as `onetsolutions_hosting_database.shop.name`. Changing it grants the user on another database (replacement).
- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting. Changing it recreates the object in the other web hosting.
- `username` (String) The name of the user, with or without the web hosting's username prefix, such as `onetsolutions_hosting_database_user.app.username`. Changing it grants another user (replacement).

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `privileges` (Set of String) The privileges granted: `ALL PRIVILEGES` (the default), or any of `ALTER`, `ALTER ROUTINE`, `CREATE`, `CREATE ROUTINE`, `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES`, `CREATE VIEW`, `DELETE`, `DROP`, `EVENT`, `EXECUTE`, `INDEX`, `INSERT`, `LOCK TABLES`, `REFERENCES`, `SELECT`, `SHOW VIEW`, `TRIGGER`, `UPDATE`. They replace the user's previous privileges on the database and can be changed in place.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The full database name and the full username, separated by a slash: `<database>/<username>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_database_privileges.app_on_shop
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/acme_shop/acme_app"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<database>/<username>, or <hosting_id>/<database>/<username>
# when the provider sets organization_id and project_id. The privileges cannot be imported: the next
# apply sets the configured ones.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_database_privileges.app_on_shop 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/5e7c2a1b-9d3f-4a6e-8b2c-1d0f9e8a7b6c/acme_shop/acme_app
```
